newsitem.title: UK: NWE gasoline prompt barges up $12 on refinery woes.
newsitem.headline: NWE gasoline prompt barges up $12 on refinery woes.

text.p: Several gasoline barge trades by Monday lunchtime confirmed a $12 rise in prompt values largely on the back of Friday's news of three unanticipated catalytic cracker outages.

Confirmation that the BP/Texaco Nerefco unit in Rotterdam was back up and operating normally Monday morning and the expectation by BP/Mobil that the joint venture's Coryton, U.K., cracker would restart during the second half of this week had yet to impact prompt gasoline sentiments.
But as talked levels began to stabilise by late morning/lunchtime, several dealers began to look to afternoon developments on the Nymex for fresh direction.

Indeed, those sentiments were fully reflected in the prompt cargo market, in which a $231 CIF NWE prompt to August 15 deal was heard for a 10,000 tonne shipment. The NWE refiner rumored to have sold the volume would not comment on the rumored deal but indicated the prompt cargo market had been making gains broadly in line with barges.

A Wall Street trader was seen heavily active in the physical market Monday, confirming three first half August Eurograde buys at $227, having earlier purchased at $224 alongside other participants' trades at $222 and $225.

August swap values were meanwhile seen rising by around $7 Monday, with a trade seen at $217.50, but September was at best talked $3 up on the day amid rumored trades in the $201-$202 range and offer talk at $202.50.
The levels reflected a widening backwardation between prompt and second half August/outer month values as second half Eurograde barges were seen just $4 up, thus losing $8 to first half August.
